title: Content refresh
content: A content refresh is an update to the facts, examples, and structure of a published page that keeps the page at its existing URL.

meta.why: The existing URL keeps the links that point to it, and readers get facts that still hold.
meta.example: A pricing guide gets new plan prices, a replaced screenshot, and a revised comparison table, then shows a new updated date.
meta.check: Review a page's dated facts, prices, and screenshots and change what is out of date. Then update the visible date and the dateModified value to match the change.
meta.limitation: Changing the date without changing the content gives a reader nothing new.
meta.sources: Google Search Central: publication dates | https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/publication-dates | Platform documentation
